biteOfDay: Cooling surface water on Table Rock has bass transitioning to deeper patterns on points, gravel flats and offshore structure in 20–40 ft as they pack on weight ahead of winter. Walleye and crappie remain active around brush piles and points. On Taneycomo, rainbows stay eager in the seams during lighter flows while brown trout activity builds in the upper stretches. tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~4,016 cfs at 15:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~4,043. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: Hit the low-flow window this morning on Taneycomo. Drift or wade seams and current breaks with 1/16–1/8 oz marabou micro jigs (black, sculpin, olive with orange head) or #16–20 zebra midges under an indicator on light line.
